title: Demystifying Backpropagation: The Matrix Calculus Behind Deep Learning

author.name: Hamid
author.role: B.Tech CS & AI Student | ML & DSA

summary: Every deep learning engineer relies on loss.backward(), but what actually happens under the hood? Here is a complete mathematical & visual breakdown of computational graphs, multivariable chain rule, Jacobians, and weight updates.
keyTakeaways: Forward pass evaluates activations layer by layer: z^(l) = W^(l)a^(l-1) + b^(l)
Backward pass propagates error gradients via multivariable chain rule
Jacobian-vector products enable memory-efficient reverse-mode differentiation
Weight updates follow the negative gradient direction: W <- W - α * (∂L/∂W)
fullArticle:
Backpropagation is often described as the backbone of modern artificial intelligence. While frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow abstract away the differentiation step with automatic gradient accumulation, mastering the underlying linear algebra and multivariable calculus is what separates good engineers from exceptional ones.

### The Computational Graph
In modern neural networks, computation is modeled as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Each node represents an operation or tensor, and edges represent tensor data flow. During the forward pass, input features x pass through affine transformations followed by non-linear activations (e.g. ReLU, GELU, Softmax).

### Reverse-Mode Automatic Differentiation
Why reverse mode instead of forward mode? If a network maps from ℝⁿ (thousands of parameters) to ℝ (a scalar loss value), reverse-mode AD computes all partial derivatives in a single backward pass with O(1) temporal overhead relative to the forward pass!

title: PyTorch vs. JAX vs. TensorFlow in 2026: An AI Student's Architectural Deep Dive

author.name: Hamid
author.role: B.Tech CS & AI Student | ML & DSA

summary: Comparing dynamic versus static execution graphs, XLA JIT-compilation, higher-order automatic differentiation (jax.grad), and GPU tensor memory benchmarks in 2026.
keyTakeaways: PyTorch remains king of debugging & developer ergonomics with dynamic eager execution
JAX treats computation as pure functions, excelling in TPU scaling and higher-order derivatives
TensorFlow / Keras 3 provides seamless cross-backend enterprise deployment
TorchDynamo & torch.compile() bridge the gap between PyTorch usability and JAX compile speed
fullArticle:
As an AI student building real-world projects from automated attendance recognition to agentic LLM workflows, choosing the right deep learning library is a critical decision.

### Dynamic vs Static Graphs
In earlier years, TensorFlow required pre-defining static computation graphs, whereas PyTorch revolutionized deep learning research by introducing dynamic eager execution (define-by-run). Today, JAX approaches the challenge through functional programming: models are written as pure Python functions transformed via jit, grad, and vmap.

### The XLA Advantage
Accelerated Linear Algebra (XLA) compiler fuses operations (like elementwise addition and activation) into single GPU kernels, drastically eliminating VRAM read/write roundtrips. PyTorch 2.x adopts this via TorchInductor, giving us the best of both worlds.

title: Geometry of High Dimensions: SVD, Eigenvectors, & PCA in Practice

author.name: Hamid
author.role: B.Tech CS & AI Student | ML & DSA

summary: Why does Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) work so magically for dimensionality reduction? Exploring orthogonal projection, spectral theorem, covariance diagonalization, and explained variance.
keyTakeaways: SVD factorizes any m×n matrix into A = U Σ V^T without requiring square dimensions
PCA seeks the orthogonal axes of maximal variance in centered data
The right singular vectors V correspond to principal directions (eigenvectors of X^T X)
Singular values in Σ directly quantify the variance explained by each principal component
fullArticle:
High-dimensional datasets suffer from the curse of dimensionality—sparsity grows exponentially, distances concentrate, and visualization becomes impossible. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) provides the elegant mathematical cure.

### Spectral Decomposition Meets SVD
While PCA is formulated around finding eigenvectors of the sample covariance matrix C = (1 / (n - 1)) * X^T X, directly computing X^T X can cause severe numerical instability when features outnumber samples.

Instead, singular value decomposition of the centered data matrix X = U Σ V^T directly yields the principal component loadings in V without explicitly materializing the covariance matrix. This mathematical insight is why Scikit-Learn's PCA implementation uses SVD under the hood!
